clues: This is the main town of a small land in Central America. It sits in a high valley in the hills, in the south part of the land.
Though it lies in the hot tropics, high land keeps it warm like spring all year. Rain falls from May to October, then dry months follow.
The Spanish built this place after a huge quake in 1773 wrecked their old capital. The quake and its shocks forced them to start fresh here.
Long ago, this spot was a Mayan town that thrived for more than two thousand years. Its people lived here from deep in the past to about 1200.
This place is the national capital and the biggest town in all of Central America. All the top work of state, faith, and trade runs through here.
